newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia says unable to join WTO infotech deal yet.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says unable to join WTO infotech deal yet.

text.p: Malaysia said on Friday it was unable to join World Trade Organisation (WTO) initiatives for a declaration on information technology products but welcomes the objective to eliminate duties on high-tech products.

"Malaysia is not able to join this initiative at this juncture, due to the need to undertake a thorough analysis of product coverage and to have the necessary internal consultations with the affected parties to decide on the products in which offers could be made," Malaysia's minister of International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz said.
Aziz said government approval will be secured for Malaysia's participation in this initiative after completion of the analysis and consultations.
The minister, however, welcomed the initiative, stating that it provides flexibility for participating countries to phase out tariffs later than the year 2000, if necessary.
"There are also provisions for expanding product coverage," she added.
Currently, 65 percent of the products proposed for coverage in this initiative are already duty free in Malaysia, Aziz said.
In 1995, Malaysia exported US$39.5 billion of information technology products while imports amounted to US$33.5 billion.

Ministers at the inaugural first ministerial meeting of the WTO in Singapore have been trying hard to reach agreement on an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) to remove barriers on computer and telecommunications products by 2000.
The pact, covering 300 product categories, was the crowning achievement of this week's ministerial meeting.

About 30 countries are due to sign the pact on Friday and many more by mid-March -- the deadline set by the United States and the European Union (EU) to sign up countries accounting for 90 percent of world trade in IT.
